correctness.rationale: The unique norming functional of a real Hilbert-valued p-sum gives exact equation (5). For a Birkhoff pair, Cauchy–Schwarz bounds its reverse residual by the explicit two-parameter envelope (9). The two pieces have strictly opposite monotonicity in block mass, so the unique optimal mass is 1/(1+τ). Blockwise collinear opposite-sign witnesses (13) attain equality for every positive ratio τ. Boundary blocks give zero, and the scalar profile has a positive attained maximum below 1 for p≠2. Hyperbolic algebra proves Hölder duality. A uniform 2z exp(−9z/14) tail bound near p=2 makes the compact convergence of normalized profiles global and identifies the unique slope maximizer z0 tanh z0=1. These are complete analytic arguments independent of numerical checks.
risks: All hypotheses are real Hilbert; p=1 and p=infinity require different norming-functional analysis. Numerical tests are not substitutes for uniform estimates.

originality.rationale: The first-public 2023 direct-sum paper was inspected through its complete 21-page preprint, including its support-functional, exact Birkhoff orthogonality and left/right symmetry theorems. Its qualitative formulas are inputs but do not give the exact C-symmetry supremum, blockwise extremizer rigidity or near-Hilbert slope. The 2021/2023 open-access two-summand source was also read through §5, and the 2020/2021 C-symmetry framework compared. Actual scientific-index and primary-literature queries covered equivalent support residuals, exact formulas, Hilbert-valued sums, p↔p′ duality and near-two asymptotics; nearest indexed results are different geometric invariants. The 2018 earlier global-constant article was accessible only via abstract, so equivalent hidden statements remain a documented residual risk; negative searches alone are not treated as novelty proof.

value.rationale: This is a sharp global quantitative classification for a canonical infinite family of real Banach spaces, independent of two arbitrarily large Hilbert-fiber dimensions. It answers the natural question raised by direct-sum Birkhoff orthogonality whether new Hilbert directions worsen the asymmetry; the answer is a precise rigidity theorem. The exact equality configurations and sharp p→2 linear defect quantify how rapidly p-sums depart from Hilbert symmetry, improving far beyond qualitative exact-versus-nonexact pointwise symmetry. The p→2 coefficient is intrinsically determined, not an arbitrary finite computation.
risks: No extension to arbitrary Banach fibers or three-plus summands has been established.
